subtopics.title: Charges Must Cancel — the One Law of Formula Writing

questions.question: The one law of formula writing is:
options: The metal is always written last
Subscripts must always be even
The compound must be electrically neutral — total positive plus total negative charge equals zero
Every formula needs brackets

questions.question: Metals form cations because they:
options: Gain electrons and become negative
Lose electrons and become positive
Share electrons equally
Never carry charge

questions.question: Aluminium chloride is AlCl3 because:
options: Aluminium is three-plus and each chloride is one-minus — three chlorides reach zero
Chlorine always takes a subscript of three
Aluminium is in period three
Three is the smallest allowed subscript

subtopics.title: Calcium Chloride and the Crossover Method

questions.question: The crossover method works by:
options: Swapping the two element symbols
Adding the two charges together
Doubling both charges before writing
Crossing each charge's size over to become the other ion's subscript

questions.question: Crossing calcium two-plus with oxide two-minus prints Ca2O2. The correct formula is:
options: Ca2O2 exactly as printed
CaO — always simplify to the smallest whole-number ratio
CaO2
Ca2O

questions.question: Safety rule two of the crossover says:
options: Always write the sign next to the subscript
Cross only the negative charge
Never write a subscript of one — CaCl2, not Ca1Cl2
Subscripts belong in front of the symbol

questions.question: The charge audit of CaCl2 gives:
options: Plus two and minus two — zero: neutral, proven
Plus two and minus one — not neutral
Plus one and minus two
Plus four and minus four

subtopics.title: Ammonium Sulphate — Polyatomic Ions and the Bracket Rule

questions.question: A polyatomic ion is:
options: Any ion with a charge bigger than one
A metal atom with extra electrons
Two separate ions written together
A charged team of atoms that travels and reacts as one unit

questions.question: Ammonium and sulphate are, with their charges:
options: NH4 one-plus and SO4 two-minus
NH3 one-plus and SO3 two-minus
NH4 one-minus and SO4 two-plus
NH4 two-plus and SO4 one-minus

questions.question: The brackets in (NH4)2SO4 are non-negotiable because without them:
options: The formula is too long to read
NH42SO4 claims forty-two hydrogens — the subscript must multiply the whole team
Sulphate would need its own brackets
The charge audit cannot be written

questions.question: The atom count of (NH4)2SO4 is:
options: One nitrogen, four hydrogens, one sulphur, four oxygens
Two nitrogens, four hydrogens, two sulphurs, eight oxygens
Two nitrogens, eight hydrogens, one sulphur, four oxygens
One nitrogen, eight hydrogens, one sulphur, eight oxygens

subtopics.title: Iron(III) Oxide — Roman Numerals and the Complete Method

questions.question: The Roman numeral in iron(III) oxide tells you:
options: The number of iron atoms in the formula
The number of oxygens in the formula
The period iron sits in
The charge of the iron ion — Fe three-plus

questions.question: Iron(III) oxide is Fe2O3 because:
options: The lowest common multiple of three and two is six — two irons at plus three cancel three oxides at minus two
Iron always takes a subscript of two
The crossover result had to be doubled
Oxygen forms three-minus ions

questions.question: Iron(II) oxide differs from iron(III) oxide in that:
options: They are the same substance written two ways
FeO and Fe2O3 are different compounds with different colours and behaviour
Only iron(III) oxide contains oxygen
Iron(II) oxide needs brackets

questions.question: Step five of the complete method is:
options: Cross the charges over
Look up the ions on the data sheet
Audit — total plus cancels total minus, and the atom count respects every bracket
Simplify the subscripts

questions.question: In the till picture, metals are the givers because they:
options: Hand out electrons and end up positive, like someone owed money
Take in electrons and end up negative
Never change their charge
Hold the drawer open

questions.question: Calcium chloride needs two chlorides because:
options: Chlorine always comes in pairs
Calcium hands out two and each chloride can take only one — the drawer closes at zero with two takers
The crossover method demands even numbers
Calcium is bigger than chlorine

questions.question: The Ca2O2 result from the swap must be cancelled down because:
options: Oxygen cannot take a subscript
Four atoms is too many for one formula
Two-for-two is one-for-one in disguise — the honest formula is CaO
The charges did not cancel

subtopics.title: The Team Rides in One Taxi

questions.question: Ammonium rides as one passenger, meaning:
options: Its five atoms travel and react together, paying a single fare of plus one
Each of its atoms carries its own charge
It splits into nitrogen and hydrogen when reacting
It always rides with a metal

questions.question: The brackets in (NH4)2SO4 are the taxi because they:
options: Separate the metal from the non-metal
Show the compound is a solid
Mark the formula as ionic
Carry the whole group so the two outside multiplies every atom inside

questions.question: Sulphate gets no bracket in ammonium sulphate because:
options: Sulphate never takes brackets in any compound
Only one sulphate travels — brackets are needed only when a group is multiplied
Sulphate is not a polyatomic ion
The formula would be too long

questions.question: The endings whisper the passenger: sulphide versus sulphate is:
options: Both the same ion written differently
Sulphide with oxygens, sulphate without
Plain S two-minus for sulphide; S O four two-minus for sulphate — the '-ate' means oxygens aboard
Sulphide positive, sulphate negative

subtopics.title: When the Name Whispers the Charge

questions.question: Iron needs a Roman numeral in its name because:
options: Iron is the heaviest common metal
All metals require numerals
The numeral counts the oxygen atoms
Iron hands out two on some days and three on others — the name must say which iron attended

questions.question: Built from scratch, iron(III) oxide comes out as:
options: Fe2O3 — two irons handing out six, three oxygens taking six, and it is rust
FeO — one of each
Fe3O2 — three irons, two oxygens
FeO3 — one iron, three oxygens

questions.question: Step four of the kitchen recipe says:
options: Write the charges above the symbols permanently
Cancel down, taxi any multiplied group, and drop every little one
Swap the symbols before the numbers
Count only the positive charges
